classification.difficultyReason: Determine a parameter from an interval, a singleton or an empty quadratic-inequality solution set.

content.prompt: Consider the quadratic inequality $x^2+4x+c\leq0$. For each of the following sets of values of $x$, find the values of $c$ for which the given set is exactly the solution set of the inequality:

answer.short:
$c=-21$.

The upward-opening parabola must have zeros at $-7$ and $3$.
answer.worked:
For the graph to be on or below the $x$-axis exactly between $-7$ and $3$, its zeros must be $-7$ and $3$. Its leading coefficient is $1$.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+4x+c&=(x+7)(x-3)\\x^2+4x+c&=x^2+4x-21\\c&=-21\end{align*}$$

With $c=-21$, the parabola opens upwards and is on or below the $x$-axis exactly when $-7\leq x\leq3$.

answer.short:
$c=4$.

The vertex must lie on the $x$-axis so that only $x=-2$ satisfies the inequality.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+4x+c\\y&=(x+2)^2+c-4\end{align*}$$

The parabola opens upwards and has vertex $(-2,c-4)$. For its graph to be on or below the $x$-axis only at $x=-2$, the vertex must lie on the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}c-4&=0\\c&=4\end{align*}$$

Then $(x+2)^2\leq0$ holds only when $x=-2$.

answer.short:
$c>4$.

The minimum value $c-4$ must be positive.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y&=x^2+4x+c\\y&=(x+2)^2+c-4\end{align*}$$

The parabola opens upwards and its minimum value is $c-4$, attained at $x=-2$. There are no solutions to $y\leq0$ precisely when the whole graph lies above the $x$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}c-4&>0\\c&>4\end{align*}$$
